Name: Stacey Ellison
Badge: Layering Reading, Writing and Thinking
How does the Layering Reading, Writing, and Discussion approach compare to how you have previously supported students in engaging with multiple texts or teaching argument writing? How might this process shift or refine the way you guide students toward forming their own claims?:

Usually when I am teaching with multi-text it is a compare and contrast situtation. I like the idea of using these as building blocks even if they don't all agree. Giving students the info/tools to form an opinion first is huge. We ask them to make choices and decisions all the time and then judge those choices because they haven't based them on anything. I have no idea why everyone isn't doing this!

How would you describe the role of talk and discussion in your classroom right now? What kinds of opportunities do students have to rehearse ideas through conversation? What challenges have you encountered in making talk a meaningful part of the writing process?:
I have students have conversation at their table or with a partner regularly. If class is silent during discussions or we are stuck on an idea. They are very good at sharing ideas with each other and willing to talk freely. I established at the beginning of the year it is okay to say "at my table we said" or "so & so said" to take pressure off of them self. The most challenging part of writing for students is getting the first words down. In the last years have started saying put down whatever words are in your head, we can make them better. They don't understand revise!
